title: Final diplomatic article-text batch derived from RHD-FR-003
transcription_scope: complete article text for the 19 remaining accepted Rarámuri→German starts in RHD-FR-003; source spelling and punctuation retained; typographic line wrapping not encoded
provenance_note: AI-assisted visual transcription from printed pp. 353–356 of the supplied Steffel facsimile. The facsimile is authoritative and OCR is only a secondary reading aid. This batch completes diplomatic coverage of every accepted start in RHD-FR-003. Cuviruſi is resolved conservatively as a cross-reference to Gries by combining the visible p. 356 string with the internal German→Rarámuri Gries article; the resolution remains explicitly pending independent human confirmation.

records.article_diplomatic: Ajóruje, zornig machen. Beleidigen. Rúje, iſt ein Hülfswort wirkender Bedeutung, und einem andern Zeitworte angehängt, bedeutet es dasjenige Thun oder Machen, was das Zeitwort ſelbſt ausdrücket.
records.uncertainty_note: The accented Rarámuri forms are retained from the facsimile; the grammatical analysis is Steffel's historical wording and remains pending independent linguistic review.

records.article_diplomatic: Aitáruc, Teufel. Gemeiniglich aber wird er Telegatigameke (der unten iſt,) genannt. Tele, unten, gatiki, ſeyn; die Endſilben ameke bezeichnen das Mittelwort gegenwärtiger Zeit wirkender Bedeutung. Die Tarahumaren verſchlingen zwar in der Ausſprache meiſtentheils die letzte Sylbe ke, ich habe ſie aber doch allen dergleichen Wörtern zugeſchrieben.
records.uncertainty_note: The article begins low in the left column and continues at the top of the right column of p. 353; historical grammatical terminology and Rarámuri morphology remain pending human/linguistic verification.

records.article_diplomatic: Amela, Man ſoll oder muß ſuchen. Mela ein Hülfswort wirkender Bedeutung, einem andern mit Verwerfung deſſen letzter Sylbe angehängt, bedeutet, daß man dieſes thun ſolle, was das Zeitwort ausdrückt, ſ. müſſen.
records.uncertainty_note: The article boundary is visually clear; historical grammatical interpretation remains pending linguistic verification.
The facsimile shows the acute mark in Balá; the machine/OCR layer had reduced this accepted start to Bala.
